title: Launch Pulse Framework: dependency harmonization & pre-flight gating for runtime, console, and API
creator: Maya Singh
description: Create a repeatable 'Launch Pulse' framework that harmonizes cross-team dependencies, pre-flight gating checks, and escalation paths for coordinated releases that touch runtime, console, and API surfaces. This ticket captures the plan, decision records, and operational checklist for the upcoming release window (Mar 2026). The goal is to reduce last-minute rollbacks by: 1) centralizing dependency signals (schema/API contract freeze, runtime kernel pin, console UI freeze), 2) defining pre-flight test matrix and smoke/stress shadowing, and 3) codifying go/no-go criteria mapped to SLOs, cost thresholds, and customer-impact tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Launch Pulse playbook published in Confluence with checklist and owner matrix
Pre-flight gating matrix agreed by eng/product/design with signoffs recorded
Automated preflight smoke job (runtime + API) exists and runs in staging with pass/fail signals in the dashboard
Rollback and fallback runbook validated in a dry-run with on-call rotation assigned
Dependencies list reconciled and capacity reservations confirmed for Dedicated pools
activity: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff meeting with runtime, console, API leads. Decisions: enforce contract freeze 72h before cut (A. Park), runtime quantization rollouts must be staged behind canaries (L. Torres).
2026-03-01 - Draft of gating matrix posted to Confluence; requested input from Security for KMS implications (J. Rivera).
2026-03-03 - Design review: console cutover banner and user-facing rollback messaging approved (S. Chen). Follow-up: include copy variations for enterprise vs self-serve flows.
2026-03-05 - Engineering noted risk: autoscaler tuning for Dedicated pools may affect canary throughput. Action: ENG-19834 to add buffer capacity, dependency added.
2026-03-08 - PM review: consolidated signals added to dashboard (latency P50/P95, error rate, token-cost drift). Request from CTO to include 'cost per 1M tokens' threshold for auto-abort.
2026-03-10 - Dry-run scheduled: smoke tests and rollback drill planned on 2026-03-15 with on-call roster confirmed.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stricter freeze window reduces regressions but may delay emergent critical patches. We agreed on a fast-path exemption process with SRE signoff.
Observation: previous launches had highest incidence of issues when runtime kernel selections changed within 48h of cut. Motion: add kernel-lock step to gating matrix.
Follow-up: add cost regression smoke tests to ensure quantization changes don't push token-cost beyond threshold.
